answer: Copying becomes a race the adversary always loses, and producing 83 original texts is the only way to fill 99 aliases; the cipher log preserves both halves. The reveal must open the same anchor hash, and a reveal that arrives late or mismatched is dropped at the dune gate. Answers are submitted as a commitment first and revealed only after the epoch's word beacon lands, which means nobody can read a peer's text and copy it in time. That is 13 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
